cpu_under_test: pynqz1_rocket_smp (2 harts, one shared 4-way 64 KiB L2, l2_banks=1)
_comment: Derived from out/rocket_membench/run.json derived.contention[rd_16777216] (both working sets past the 64 KiB L2, the plateau the measured curve settles on from 256 KiB up).  NOT a per-kernel co-run measurement: it is a STREAMING microbenchmark, so applying its bandwidth-retention reciprocal to a whole kernel's service time charges the compute fraction as if it were memory too.  That direction is pessimistic and deliberate -- it is an upper bound on the contention penalty, not an estimate of it.  It is also unconditional: XPU-RT applies the factor per (op, combination), so a dispatch is charged even in a stretch where the other lane happens to be idle.  A per-dispatch paired solo/co-run arm on these two workloads is what would replace it.

same_cluster._note: this SoC has ONE cluster; both harts share the one L2, so every singleton combination is same_cluster
